AI Mindfulness Guide

A gentle guide for short pauses in a busy day: breathing exercises, grounding, body scans and evening reflection. It meets you where you are and keeps practices short enough to actually do.

TL;DR
  • Best for 2–10 minute breathing, grounding and reflection exercises.
  • Tell it how you feel right now and how much time you have.
  • It is a self-help tool, not therapy; in a crisis, contact emergency services.
Not therapy, not medical advice

This AI coach is a self-help tool. It is not a licensed psychologist, therapist or doctor, and it cannot diagnose or treat anything. If you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, call your local emergency number now (112, 911 or 999 in many countries) or find a free, confidential helpline at findahelpline.com.

What this coach helps with

  • Calming down before a meeting or exam
  • Short breathing and grounding exercises
  • A body scan before sleep
  • Evening reflection and gratitude
  • Building a small daily practice

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my mindfulness guide. I feel [feeling] and have [minutes] minutes. Guide me through one short exercise, one step at a time.

  2. Walk me through a 4-7-8 breathing exercise and tell me when to switch, slowly.

  3. I have an important [meeting, exam] in 10 minutes and my heart is racing. Give me a 2-minute calming routine.

  4. Guide me through a 5-4-3-2-1 grounding exercise. Wait for my answer after each step.

  5. Lead a 5-minute body scan to help me fall asleep. Use slow, simple sentences.

  6. Ask me three gentle evening questions to reflect on my day without judging myself.

  7. Create a 7-day beginner mindfulness plan with one 5-minute practice a day.

  8. I keep replaying [situation] in my head. Suggest a short exercise to notice the thought and let it pass.

  9. Turn [daily activity, e.g. washing dishes] into a one-minute mindfulness practice.

  10. Explain the difference between mindfulness and meditation in plain words, with one exercise for each.

  11. I get distracted after 30 seconds of meditating. Give me three tips and a 1-minute practice for beginners.

  12. Write a short, calm script I can read to myself when I feel overwhelmed at work.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExampleTwo minutes before a presentation

YouI'm presenting in 10 minutes and I'm shaking.

Mindfulness GuideThat's your body getting ready, not failing you. Let's slow it down. Breathe in through your nose for 4 counts, hold for 2, and breathe out through your mouth for 6. Do that five times. Then press your feet into the floor and notice three things you can see. How do you feel now?

ExampleA busy mind at night

YouI can't sleep, my mind keeps going over tomorrow's tasks.

Mindfulness GuideLet's give those thoughts a place to go. Take a minute to write tomorrow's tasks on paper, then close the notebook. Now lie back and bring your attention to your toes. Notice their weight. Slowly move up to your feet, your ankles, your calves. If a thought comes, label it “planning” and return to your body.

Tips for better answers

  • Say how much time you have. A one-minute practice you do beats a 20-minute one you skip.
  • Ask the guide to wait for your reply after each step, so it feels like a real session.
  • Try the same exercise for a week before deciding it doesn't work.
  • If difficult feelings come up and stay, talk to someone you trust or a professional.

Questions people ask

Can an AI guide me through meditation?

Yes, for simple practices. An AI mindfulness guide can lead breathing exercises, body scans and grounding techniques step by step, adjusting to how much time you have. It works best when you ask it to pause after each step. For deeper or long-term practice, many people also learn from a teacher or a course.

Is mindfulness with an AI a replacement for therapy?

No. Mindfulness exercises can help with everyday stress, but they are not treatment for anxiety, depression or trauma. The AI guide is not a therapist and cannot assess your health. If you feel unsafe or overwhelmed for weeks, talk to a doctor or mental health professional, or call emergency services.

How long should a daily mindfulness practice be?

Start with two to five minutes a day. Consistency matters more than length, and a short practice is easier to keep. Many people tie it to something they already do, like the first coffee or the walk home. After a few weeks you can extend it if it feels useful.

What is a good first exercise for a beginner?

Box breathing is an easy start: breathe in for four counts, hold for four, breathe out for four, hold for four, and repeat for two minutes. It needs no equipment and works anywhere. Ask the guide to count with you slowly and check in with you at the end.
